question: What is the primary goal of injection safety monitoring in a healthcare facility?

options.C: Reducing the cost of hospital drugs

explanation: Monitoring injection practices primarily aims to safeguard patients and staff from bloodborne pathogens and accidental injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why are bloodborne viruses a major concern during unsafe injections?

options.B: They spread rapidly through contaminated needles
options.C: They only affect nurses in rural clinics

explanation: Reusing needles or poor disposal transfers pathogens directly into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h1)

question: How often must the injection safety monitoring form be completed?
explanation: The tool is specifically designed for a monthly review of device stock and usage patterns. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h2)

question: What happens when physical inventory is reconciled with patient attendance records?

options.A: Doctor consultation fees are automatically calculated
options.B: Discrepancies and potential device theft or waste are exposed
options.C: Patient admission registers are permanently closed
options.D: Unused medication expires on the hospital shelf

explanation: Comparing used items against patient numbers confirms that devices are used strictly for clinical care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h2)

question: Which item belongs in the facility information section of the form?
explanation: The header section identifies where the data originated, such as the emergency room or maternity ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why is recording the closing balance important on an inventory form?

options.A: It serves as the opening balance for the next month
options.B: It calculates the total electricity consumed
options.C: It proves that zero patients visited the hospital
options.D: It determines the salary of the ward storekeeper

explanation: Accurate closing stock ensures continuity and prevents discrepancies in subsequent monthly reports. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is the special feature of an auto-disable syringe?

options.A: It administers two drugs at once
options.B: It locks or breaks after one use
options.C: It does not require a needle attached
options.D: It can be sterilized in boiling water

explanation: Auto-disable mechanisms prevent healthcare workers from accidentally or intentionally reusing the same syringe. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why must safety boxes be puncture-resistant?

options.A: To allow them to hold liquid waste without leaking
options.B: To prevent needles from piercing through and injuring handlers
options.C: To ensure they can be washed and reused multiple times
options.D: To make them light enough to carry around the ward

explanation: Solid walls protect waste handlers and cleaners from accidental needle pricks during collection and transport. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h4)

question: When should the data for the monthly report be gathered?

options.A: During the annual hospital accreditation visit
options.B: At the close of the final day of the month
options.C: In the middle of the first working week
options.D: Whenever the ward store runs completely empty

explanation: Timing compilation to month-end captures a full calendar month of accurate utilization data. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h5)

question: A nurse discovers a discrepancy between recorded usage and physical stock. What is the appropriate next step?

options.A: Discard the monitoring form and start a fresh one
options.B: Blame the incoming shift for losing the supplies
options.C: Ignore the difference if it is less than ten items
options.D: Investigate tally sheets and recount the remaining stock

explanation: Thorough checks of raw tally sheets and physical inventory resolve errors before official submission. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common error found during form audits?

options.A: Missing signatures of the reporting officer
options.D: Transposed numbers in the tally column

explanation: Accurate math represents a successful compilation, whereas transposed numbers, missing signatures, and omitted items are typical errors. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why should ward register totals be cross-verified with pharmacy store records?

options.A: To confirm that distributed supplies match documented clinical usage
options.B: To reduce the number of patients admitted to the ward
options.C: To ensure the pharmacy staff finish their shift on time
options.D: To calculate the profit made from selling injection devices

explanation: Comparing pharmacy issues with ward usage confirms accountability and prevents inventory diversion. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h6)

question: Who receives the completed monthly injection safety report from the ward focal person?
explanation: Infection control officers coordinate safety data collection and review across hospital departments. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is the impact of submitting monthly safety reports late?

options.A: It improves the accuracy of the upcoming year budget
options.B: It stops patients from visiting the outpatient clinic
options.C: It delays procurement and can cause critical stockouts
options.D: It automatically increases the delivery speed of goods

explanation: Central medical stores depend on timely facility reports to forecast needs and replenish depleted stocks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h7)
